messages:
marie: Quick brain-dump: prototype for 'progressive-tile loader' (different from index-first). We store each shard as a sequence of fixed-size tiles (1MB tile default) with a small TileMap sidecar that maps tensor->tile-range. Warmup pulls tiles by heatmap rather than contiguous byte ranges. Goal: bounded number of small reads, predictable memory increments, easier compression alignment.

devin: tile size 1MB seems reasonable. How do tiles map to tensor boundaries? safetensors needs contiguous arrays; tiles could split tensors.

marie: TileMap stores (tensor_name, tile_start_idx, tile_end_idx, tensor_offset_in_first_tile). If a tensor spans tiles we stitch during commit. Reader fetches full tiles (no partial-tile reads) so compressed transports map to whole compressed chunks easily.

alejandro: how do we compute heatmap? runtime-access telemetry? token-affinity?

marie: two inputs: (1) static profile from evals/prompt-sets indicating layer access order for common prompts and (2) online short-term histogram of recent KV lookups (last 100 requests). We merge with decay weights to pick top-K tiles per shard to prefetch.

kevin: that helps for prefix-heavy workloads. But what about generative multi-turns where accesses jump across layers and attention windows?

marie: we make it multi-phase: initial seed tiles = tile 0..N (small), then short-term heatmap drives phase-2 prefetch. Also a fallback: if a tile miss causes hot path eviction thrash, escalate to shard-hotstart for that model version.

alejandro: atomicity and verification? we need to avoid partial tensor exposure and keep reproducibility.

marie: every tile has a SHA256 tag in TileMap. Tiles fetched into per-request staging area and verified before merging into the global tile-cache. Merge is atomic via an epoched cache map so readers never see partial tiles. We also store a model-versioned tile manifest to ensure determinism across nodes.

kevin: interactions with quantized layouts and sparsity? Tiles might mix quantized subarrays.

marie: tile content is just raw bytes; the loader tracks tensor metadata (dtype, shape, quant_meta) in the TileMap. When merging tiles we annotate which tile contains Q-meta to let the runtime pick correct kernels. For sparse formats we keep a sparse-index sidecar which the tile loader consults; sparse tiles can be skipped if access not needed.

devin: compression story?

marie: prefer block-compressed container (zstd frames per tile). Since tiles align with compression frames, partial reads are cheap. For legacy gzip blobs we fall back to chunk-granularity addressing and tile-size becomes multiple-of-chunk. TileMap indicates addressing_mode: {raw, compressed_frame, chunked}.

alejandro: network load: prefetching many tiles across many concurrent requests could overload storage. Any aggregation/backpressure?

marie: yes: central warmup-aggregator coalesces identical tile requests across ephemeral requests in a 10ms window. Also we use a per-shard concurrency cap and token-bucket rate-limit per model. If we see >p95 prefetch-latency we degrade to seed-only mode. Telemetry triggers: tile.prefetch.fallback_rate, tile.verify_failures, tile.prefetch_bytes.

kevin: migration / registry compatibility? not all bundles will have TileMap.

marie: TileMap is optional sidecar: file.safetensors.tilemap.json. Registry will generate on upload on the fly. Devices without TileMap use existing index-first or full-hotstart. We include a small 'tileizer' binary that slices safetensors into tiles and emits TileMap.

ci-bot: ci-note: new unit tests required: tile-stitching, compressed-frame addressing, tilemap-backcompat. Ticket created: ML-2042.

marie: rollout plan: alpha behind feature-flag per-model; opt-in manifest field: "loader: progressive_tile_v1". Start in eng-nonprod with two canary models (small & 8-shard LLaMA-family). Monitor top-line SLOs: first_token_latency, median_token_latency, disk_io_ops, and tile.prefetch.fallback_rate.

devin: QA checklist: deterministic seeding (seed same tiles across runs), tile-corruption injection tests (bad checksum), concurrency storm sim (1000 concurrent small requests), eviction-mixed-workload test (tile churn).

alejandro: logging: include tile_id, shard_id, request_affinity, fetch_mode. Useful for debugging hotstart pathologies.

marie: open question: should tile-size be per-shard or global? I'm leaning per-shard via histogram packing: small tensors -> smaller tile-size for micro-tensors, large tensors -> larger tiles to reduce stitch overhead. Might be added in v2.

kevin: sounds solid. Please add perf microbench: bytes_read vs first_token_latency for seed-size variations (16KB, 128KB, 1MB).

marie: will do. I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with TileMap schema, Tileizer CLI, metrics list, and a minimal PoC. Thanks all :memo:
